newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy August new car registrations seen well down.
newsitem.headline: Italy August new car registrations seen well down.

text.p: Italian new car registrations in August, due to be announced on Tuesday, are expected to be well down on the same month last year, sector analysts said.
Against the 79,953 registrations in August 1995, estimates for last month see a fall of between four and 10 percent.

July new car registrations rose 0.85 percent year-on-year to 157,000 units, the ministry of transport said. In the first seven months of this year registrations totalled 1.152 million, down 0.27 percent on the same period last year.
"The trend is negative for August with even gloomier prospects for the rest of the year," said Giamprimo Quagliano, director of the Centro Studi Promotor forecasting body.
He said it was becoming ever more vital for the government to introduce some form of tax incentives to encourage car purchases "to put an end to a situation which is getting really worrying."
For the whole of 1996 Quagliano said it was "very probable" that total registrations would be below 1.7 million units against 1.726 million in 1995.

Several industrial sources forecast a fall in August new registrations of around 10 percent year-on-year to 72,000, "with a decline proportionately greater for foreign marques than for Italy's Fiat group," one analyst said.
Giampaolo Trasi of Milan broker IMI-Sigeco saw a more contained fall of around 3.5 to 4.0 percent to 77,000 units.

"The negative market trend is still continuing but I don't think the fall in August will be more than four percent," he said, adding he was sceptical about the possibility the car market getting a boost from tax incentives.

"I don't believe there will be any incentives of a fiscal nature apart from perhaps the indirect incentive of more frequent obligatory car safety checkups which would tend to speed up the replacement of old vehicles," he said.
For the whole of 1996, "we see a fall to 1.7 million units, two percent down on 1995, but we expect a three percent improvement in 1997 and a rise to 1.9 million in 1998," Trasi added.

Piero Evangelisti, spokesman for Volvo Italia, was also pessimistic for the coming months, saying that for the whole of 1996, "1.65 million registrations could be a realistic figure but it could also be worse. People are still very cautious, a lot are looking in the showrooms but not a lot are buying."
Alone among those polled to go against the trend, Ilaria Fornari, economist at JP Morgan in Milan, forecast for August a 1.5 percent rise in new registrations to 81,500 units.
